result.title: A Framework for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification under Dataset Shift
result.summary: Graph node quantification is the supervised learning task of estimating the prevalence of different classes within an arbitrary sample of unlabelled nodes from a graph, subject to some form of dataset shift. Existing approaches to graph node quantification typically follow the standard aggregative paradigm, i.e., they use labelled nodes from the graph to train an intermediate node classifier, and obtain an estimated class distribution for the sample by aggregating the classifier's predictions for the individual nodes and then correcting the result via some adjustment strategy that accounts for dataset shift. In this work we propose a framework for graph node quantification that does away with both node-level supervision, since its training phase only requires node samples labelled by their class distribution, and node-level predictions, since it estimates class prevalence values directly, without the need of any intermediate node classifier. The framework thus allows symmetric quantification, since (unlike in standard ``asymmetric'' quantification methods) the labelled items used for training and the unlabelled items on which predictions must be issued are of the same type (i.e., node samples). This framework (that we dub GSQ, for Graph Node Symmetric Quantification) allows building pipelines consisting of a node encoder, an embedding pooler, a prevalence predictor, and an optional post-hoc scaling step. These components can be instantiated by choosing from different trainable and reservoir-based encoders, different pooling operators, and different prediction objectives. We evaluate the GSQ framework on binary and multi-class datasets with different levels of homophily, under prior probability shift and under structural covariate shift.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GSQ 框架用于数据集偏移下的图节点量化：训练仅需按类别分布标注的节点样本，不需节点级分类器，而是由编码器、池化器、流行度预测器和可选事后缩放直接估计样本的类别比例，并在不同同质性与偏移条件下评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「集合级分布监督＋池化后直接输出比例」的思路或可类比 LVR 中的证据聚合与答案分布校准问题，但论文不涉及视觉输入与 latent 推理机制，属较远领域线索，需较多核查。
